solution_options.fusion_note: Low-level data fusion where the synchronized NIR and Raman spectra are merged into a single augmented matrix from the same measurement spot, requiring individual calibration blocks that must outperform single-method accuracy.

citations.quote: Data processing for pharmaceutical tasks relies on "low-level data fusion," where the synchronized NIR and Raman spectra are merged into a single augmented matrix.

chemometrics_note: Partial Least Squares (PLS) regression models combined with scatter correction are required to convert NIR spectra into quantitative API concentration values.
realtime_tracking_note: In-line fiber probes capture spectra at high speeds without interrupting production flow in the tablet press feed frame.
future_direction: Integration of validated chemometric models into automated feed-forward control systems.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If single-method NIR reflection fails to achieve required precision due to matrix interference, the extended NIR-Raman combination should be tested.
proposal.next_step: Conduct multi-method laboratory trials with representative powder blend samples and independent reference assays.

brief_answer: A fiber-based NIR reflection measurement in the tablet press feed frame is recommended as the primary option to monitor API concentration changes. Literature precedent supports NIR for pharmaceutical blend potency tracking. A preliminary pilot should test NIR reflection against independent reference laboratory assays, with a combined NIR-Raman approach held as an extended option if higher molecular specificity is required.
